name: Liechtenstein
summary_text: Liechtenstein is workable for trans visitors — safe in practice, thin in law. Same-sex relations are legal and discrimination based on sexual orientation is banned, but gender identity, gender expression, and sex characteristics are not included in any anti-discrimination legislation, and there is no legal gender recognition law. These are resident-facing gaps: a visitor faces no legal exposure. Liechtenstein is a very small, very low-crime Alpine country closely integrated with Switzerland; there is no documented pattern of anti-trans violence, no bathroom law, and no border friction (Schengen via Switzerland/Austria). Social attitudes are conservative but not mobilised-hostile. Caveat: very small population — the evidence base is thin, so this assessment carries greater-than-usual uncertainty.

sources.title: Liechtenstein | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): mixed situation - same-sex relations legal and sexual-orientation discrimination banned, but gender identity/expression/sex characteristics not covered by any anti-discrimination law; no legal gender marker change; IGM not prohibited; marriage and joint adoption available since January 2025; the state religion is Roman Catholicism and the archbishop publicly opposed marriage equality; first Pride in 2022.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 401); the underlying Reuters feature covers tiny European states (including Liechtenstein) playing catch-up on LGBT equality.

sources.title: Austria to lower hurdles for LGBT+ citizens to donate blood | Euronews
sources.claim_summary: Euronews (May 2022): Austria to lower hurdles for LGBT citizens to donate blood - regional context relevant to Liechtenstein's customs-union neighbour (page largely navigation content at fetch time).

sources.title: Gay Life in Liechtenstein - GlobalGayz
sources.claim_summary: GlobalGayz 'Gay Life in Liechtenstein' (March 2012): with a population of ~35,000 there is no organised gay scene - friendship networks are the scene; 'few organized enemies... no religious extremists, no right-wing skinheads, no political rogues demanding homophobic laws'; gay people live comfortably with little interference.

sources.title: Le prince s'en prend aux homoparents – 360°
sources.claim_summary: 360° magazine (Jan 2016, in French): Prince Hans-Adam II called rainbow families 'irresponsible' in his New Year interview, said children have 'a right to a normal family', and suggested Liechtenstein could 'ignore' an adverse European Court of Human Rights ruling; local LGBT organisation Flay said it was 'choqué'; the Freie Liste called the remarks contrary to the Constitution and the ECHR.

Landtag motion (Sept 2022, in German): 'Motion zur Öffnung der Ehe für alle' - MPs' motion to open civil marriage regardless of gender and sexual orientation, removing all remaining legal differences; notes registered partnerships are seen as a 'second-class marriage' and that the Prince had said in 2021 he had nothing against marriage equality except adoption.
